name: Running back wheel
seenIn: Covered in Football 101, Lesson 56: Running backs as receivers: the swing, the angle, the wheel and the checkdown (and why McCaffrey had 161 receiving yards)
what: The wheel is a pass to the running back where he starts out toward the sideline like a short swing pass, then turns and sprints straight up the sideline. The quarterback throws it deep over his shoulder.

At the snap the back heads for the flat, the open area near the sideline just past the line. The linebacker covering him runs over to stop a short catch. Then the back turns upfield, and the linebacker, built to stop runs, can't keep up. A receiver on that side often runs inside first to pull his cornerback out of the way.
Teams call it to get their fastest back matched against a slower linebacker in open space. When it works it's a huge play, like Christian McCaffrey's 74- and 66-yard touchdowns.

caption: White = offense, yellow = defense: the running back (RB) runs to the flat, then turns up the sideline (WHEEL); the dashed white line is the throw, and yellow dashes show the linebacker chasing the flat and the cornerback following the receiver inside.
spot: Watch the back after the snap: if he swings out toward the sideline and then keeps running straight upfield instead of stopping to catch a short pass, it's the wheel. Usually a linebacker is chasing a step or two behind him.
beats: Beats man coverage where a linebacker has to cover the back, and blitzes that leave the flat empty. Log it as Pass in the drill.
